linkedinPhoto.promptDefault:
Transform this casual selfie into a polished, corporate-grade LinkedIn headshot.

Identity preservation: Maintain the subject's exact facial structure, skin tone, eye color, hair color and style, and all distinguishing features — the result must be unmistakably the same person.

Lighting: Simulate a three-point studio setup — soft key light at 45° camera-left, gentle fill light camera-right, and a subtle rim/hair light to separate the subject from the background. Avoid harsh shadows or blown-out highlights.

Background: Clean, slightly out-of-focus neutral gradient (light grey to soft blue-grey). No distracting elements.

Composition: Tight head-and-shoulders crop, subject centered, eyes at upper-third line. Slight 10-15° body angle toward camera-left with face turned back toward camera for a natural editorial feel.

Attire & grooming: Refine clothing to appear neat and professional. Smooth minor skin blemishes while preserving natural skin texture — do not over-retouch.

Technical quality: Ultra-sharp focus on the eyes, shallow depth of field (f/2.8 equivalent), no chromatic aberration, no noise. Output resolution should match or exceed the input image.

Mood: Confident, approachable, and trustworthy — appropriate for senior professional or executive branding.

descriptions.go_fundamentals: Assess Go mechanisms, concurrency, runtime behavior, memory, and performance analysis beyond memorization.
descriptions.backend_fundamentals: Assess networking, operating systems, API design, concurrency, and backend fundamentals.
descriptions.middleware_database: Assess databases, caches, queues, middleware mechanisms, failures, and trade-offs.
descriptions.project_deep_dive: Probe real résumé projects for constraints, ownership, decisions, outcomes, and lessons.
descriptions.system_scenario: Use role-specific design or incident scenarios to assess decomposition, evidence, trade-offs, and execution.
descriptions.communication_pressure: Assess conflict communication, pressure decisions, cross-team work, and responses to challenge.
descriptions.hr_motivation: Assess motivation, career choices, stability, growth goals, and role fit.
descriptions.general_communication: Can they make something complex land with a specific audience — conclusion first, calibrated to the listener, compressed when needed? Then probe how they respond when someone more senior disagrees. Ask about a concrete episode, not "how good is your communication".
descriptions.general_logic: Give a messy, under-specified problem and watch them decompose it: state assumptions out loud, order hypotheses by likelihood and cost to check, and say what evidence would falsify each branch. No brainteasers.
descriptions.general_stress: Probe real high-pressure episodes — an incident they owned, a deadline cut in half, two managers demanding opposite things. Then push back once to see whether they hold their reasoning or fold immediately.
descriptions.general_learning: Probe the most recent thing they had to learn under time pressure: the deadline, the path from zero to shipping, what they got wrong first. Judge the method, not a list of courses watched.
descriptions.frontend_fundamentals: Check real command of HTML/CSS/JS and their framework: rendering and layout mechanics, state management, component boundaries, locating performance bottlenecks. Require links to concrete project symptoms and numbers, not API recall.
descriptions.browser_network: Probe the rendering pipeline, event loop, caching and resource loading, HTTP/2/3, CORS and security policy. The bar is explaining production symptoms (slow first paint, blank screen, duplicate requests) from mechanism, with a way to verify.
descriptions.engineering_practice: Probe engineering delivery: build and artifacts, dependency governance, canary and rollback, monitoring and alerting, test layering, review and collaboration norms. Ask why they decided that, not which tools they used.
descriptions.data_processing: Probe reliability of the data path: collection semantics, cleaning and dedup, batch vs streaming trade-offs, idempotency and backfill, data-quality checks, cost control. Require choices justified against scale and latency requirements.
descriptions.algorithm_complexity: Probe complexity reasoning and trade-offs: time vs space, where each structure fits, the cost of approximate vs exact, offline vs online consistency. Role-relevant scenarios, not whiteboard puzzles.
descriptions.metrics_experiment: Probe metric definition and experiment design: how the north-star metric is chosen, AB splitting and significance, how they attribute a metric move, causal vs correlational. Require one real judgement call and its cost.
descriptions.testing_strategy: Probe test layering and where they invest: unit/integration/e2e boundaries, flaky-test handling, fixtures and stubs, coverage against risk. Ask what they deliberately decided not to test, and why.
descriptions.cicd_delivery: Probe the delivery path: build caching and parallelism, environment parity, artifacts and versioning, canary and rollback, release risk control, rollback drills. Focus on what happens when it fails, not the happy path.
descriptions.observability_incident: Probe observability and incident handling: logs/metrics/traces trade-offs, alert quality, SLOs and error budgets, the path from symptom to root cause, mitigation and postmortem. Require the full arc of one real incident.
